subject: Hop-by-hop path skew during large syncs — NAT port contention + MTU blackhole
messages:
From: Laila Ahmed <laila@greengrid.net>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: GreenGrid Network Eng Team <ops@greengrid.net>
Date: 2027-04-02T16:10:00-07:00
Subject: Intermittent private connectivity — large-sync failures

Hi Hannah,

We started seeing failed nightly database syncs to the Redwood private node in our VPC on Monday night. Small requests succeed, but large payloads (DB snapshots ~120MB) hang during the TCP handshake or abruptly terminate mid-transfer. We retried with scp and rsync; behavior is inconsistent — sometimes a retry works, sometimes it stalls and needs an L4 connection kill to recover.

Symptoms we've captured:
- Client-side: long stalls during data push, TCP window stays small, retransmits spike.
- Ping/traceroute sometimes shows last hop responding intermittently; other times the trace stops one hop before the Redwood edge.
- We temporarily saw connection recoveries if we lowered the payload chunk size \u2014 suspect MTU/MSS issues or a middlebox dropping DF packets.

I've attached our tcpdump and a set of traceroutes (greengrid-trace-20270402.pcap + traceroutes). Can you triage? Our maintenance window is Thu 04/08 02:00-04:00 UTC if you need a coordinated test.

Thanks,
Laila Ahmed
NetOps Lead, GreenGrid Health

I'll loop in Karthik for kernel/MTU/NAT observations and Vanessa for SG/edge policy checks. If we confirm MTU blackhole signs, we may want to enable MSS clamp on the egress router and loosen any DF-dropping middlebox rules.

Attached: greengrid-traceroutes.txt (multiple runs), router-config-branch-3.txt.
Notes from our side:
- Edge NAT: we SNAT client traffic to a 10.8.0.0/24 pool on egress (branch-level). Redwood receives connections to the private endpoint and uses its own SNAT for return traffic based on the session.
- PMTU tests: ping -M do -s 1472 -> fragmented at hop 6 in ~30% of runs; most runs time out after hop 6.
- We don't have any intentional DF-dropping policies, but we do run an off-box L7 appliance that historically has dropped packets with DF combined with unexpected retransmits. We can bypass it for a test.

Subject: Re: Intermittent private connectivity — large-sync failures

Folks, quick read of the attachments and early theory:

Observations:
- Traceroutes that stop at hop 6 + PMTU fragmentation at the same hop are classic signs of an MTU blackhole or an ACL/middlebox silently dropping fragments/DF packets.
- The tcpdump shows MSS negotiation at ~1460 but we also see many retransmits and repeated SYNs where the client reattempts with new ephemeral ports.
- There's a suspicious pattern where multiple sessions from different GreenGrid clients are reusing ephemeral source ports after NAT translation (SNAT pool exhaustion + port reuse). When SNAT port collision happens, the backend sees packets out-of-order for an existing 5-tuple and drops them, which looks like abrupt connection termination.

Immediate mitigations to try during the maintenance window:
1) Expand the SNAT ephemeral range on the GreenGrid egress (increase port pool) to avoid port reuse collisions.
2) Enable MSS clamping to 1400 on the GreenGrid egress and/or on the Redwood edge for that peer to avoid DF-triggered fragmentation.
3) Temporarily bypass the L7 appliance for the test path (exclude sync flows) to rule out DF/fragment dropping.
4) Temporarily allow ICMP type 3/code 4 (fragmentation needed) on any SG/ACL between the sites so PMTU discovery can work.

Longer-term: consider sticky SNAT (per-source) for high-volume syncs or move large-sync flows over an alternate path with explicit jumbo/MSS settings.

Can we schedule a coordinated test Thu 04/08 02:30 UTC? I'll prepare a small probe script that runs iterative pings and full-size rsyncs and capture the server-side pcap concurrently.

- Karthik
SRE, Redwood Inference

Thanks Karthik, Hannah.

We can do Thu 04/08 02:30 UTC. Action items on our side:
- Increase SNAT pool on the branch (we'll allocate an additional /27 ephemeral range for syncs)
- Bypass the L7 appliance for the 30-minute test window
- Add ICMP frag-needed exceptions to the ACLs for the specific Redwood peer IPs

Question: will Redwood enable MSS clamp on the private endpoint or should we rely on our egress to do it? We'd prefer Redwood to clamp on the edge if possible so we don't need to touch every branch.

Also, please confirm whether session-affinity is required for the sync flows. If we ask our load balancer to maintain source persistence, will Redwood see consistent SNAT tuples?

Laila/Tom/Karthik team,

Plan confirmed for Thu 2027-04-08 02:30 UTC (maintenance window booked). Summary of agreed runbook:

1) GreenGrid will:
  - Expand SNAT ephemeral pool on branch -> +/27 dedicated for sync flows
  - Bypass L7 appliance for the test
  - Add ICMP type 3/code 4 allow for Redwood peer IPs
  - Kick off rsync test and keep client-side tcpdump running

2) Redwood will:
  - Enable MSS clamp to 1400 on the private-edge interface for the GreenGrid peer during the window (will revert after validation)
  - Enable verbose tcpdump capture on the private node and monitor for out-of-order packets and SYN collisions
  - If MSS clamp alone doesn't stop stalls, we'll try sticky-SNAT for sync sessions and coordinate cutover.

3) Success criteria:
  - Full DB snapshot completes without mid-transfer TCP resets for 3 consecutive runs
  - No sustained SYN collisions or ephemeral reuse observed during the test window

I've created a shared drive folder and a temporary Jira ticket (NETOPS-4982) for artifacts and postmortem. Links: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/1A2bGreengrid-sync-traces

If anything changes before Thu, flag it in the Jira and loop me in. We'll join the call at 02:25 UTC for a quick pre-test alignment.

Thanks everyone.
